_note: Indicative values, checked October 2026. Each block says where its numbers come from. Tariffs are the least certain: Indian home tariffs are slab-based with fuel surcharges, so one number per state is an approximation (see tariffBasis).

panel.source: Common 550 Wp 144 half-cell mono module, 2278 x 1134 mm (e.g. Sun Gold SG-550WM, Canadian Solar CS6W-550MB-AG datasheets)

subsidy.source: PM Surya Ghar CFA: Rs 30,000/kW up to 2 kW, Rs 18,000 for the 3rd kW, capped at Rs 78,000; residential grid-connected only (JBVNL CFA structure; Business Today, 28 Jul 2026). Confirm on pmsuryaghar.gov.in

cost.source: Gives Rs 1.7-2.2 lakh for 3 kW before subsidy. 2026 installer guides quote Rs 1.6-2.5 lakh for 3 kW DCR systems, typically Rs 55,000-65,000/kW all-in. Indicative; ask for itemised quotes

loan.source: PM Surya Ghar collateral-free loan up to Rs 2 lakh, up to 10 years. Govt reference rate repo + 0.5% (5.75%, Jul 2026); banks quote about 7-7.9%, so 7% is used. Rate is floating

co2.source: CEA CO2 Baseline Database v21.0 (Nov 2025): all-India weighted average 0.710 tCO2/MWh for FY 2024-25

defaults.source: Fallback when the state is unknown: a typical Indian urban residential rate. Yield fallback is a typical Indian value; PVGIS replaces it for the real location

tariffBasis: states[].avgTariff = rupees per unit on the top slab a household using about 300 units a month pays, including the main fuel/power-purchase surcharge where known. Solar replaces those top units first, so this is what each unit saved is worth. topUpPerKw/topUpCap = state subsidy on top of the central one.

DL.name: Delhi
DL.source: DERC FY 2025-26 slabs Rs 3.00 (0-200), 4.50 (201-400), 6.50 (401-800) plus PPAC of about 36% (BSES/TPDDL). Delhi state top-up Rs 10,000/kW up to Rs 30,000, approved by the Delhi cabinet on 20 May 2025 (Mercom, Tribune). Note: homes under 200 units already get free power, so they save less

HR.name: Haryana
HR.source: HERC FY 2025-26 order raised low slabs to Rs 2.20-2.95; higher-slab rates not confirmed (third-party calculators give Rs 6.30-7.10 above 150 units)

UP.name: Uttar Pradesh
UP.source: UPERC kept 2024-25 rates for 2025; domestic slabs Rs 3.35-6.50, about Rs 6.00 for 151-300 units urban (housing.com, Desi Utility)

RJ.name: Rajasthan
RJ.source: RERC Oct 2025 order: 301-500 units cut to Rs 7.00, above 500 to Rs 7.50; first 300 units unchanged (Mercom)

GJ.name: Gujarat
GJ.source: GERC RGP schedule w.e.f. 1 Apr 2025; third-party figures give about Rs 5.00 above 250 units, plus a variable FPPAS surcharge set by formula

MH.name: Maharashtra
MH.source: MSEDCL: energy charge about Rs 6.1-6.5 for 101-300 units plus wheeling charge, FAC and electricity duty (final MERC review order 25 Mar 2026); sources conflict

KA.name: Karnataka
KA.source: KERC 3-year order (2025-28) cut domestic energy charge by 10 paise; 201-500 units about Rs 7.0-8.35 by source. Many homes under 200 units get free power (Gruha Jyothi), so they save less

TN.name: Tamil Nadu
TN.source: TNERC LT I-A, billed every two months, revised 1 Jul 2025 (+3.16%). Slabs rise steeply above 500 units per two months; 2026 scheme rates Rs 4.70 (201-400) and 6.30 (401-500)
